newsitem.title: USA: Equitable Q1 life and annuity earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Equitable Q1 life and annuity earnings up.

text.p: Equitable Cos Inc said first quarter after-tax operating earnings from its life insurance and annuity operations rose 13 percent to $77 million from $68.1 million a year ago.

"The primary driver of our ongoing improvement in insurance operations earnings is higher fee income, reflecting growth in the separate account assets backing our variable products," said William T. McCaffrey, senior executive vice president and chief operating officer of The Equitable Life Assurance Society.

Excluded from the 1997 results are after-tax investment gains, net of deferred acquisition cost amortization (DAC) and related expenses, of $10.3 million and after-tax restructuring charges of $3.4 million.
The 1996 amount excludes after-tax investment losses of $9.3 million, net of DAC and related expenses, and $0.5 million of after-tax restructuring charges.
McCaffrey said Equitable also was pleased with the sales momentum that began early in 1996.
New variable and interest sensitive life insurance premiums advanced 32 percent during the first quarter, rising to $112.4 million versus $85.1 million a year ago.
In addition, new individual annuity premiums and deposits rose 27 percent for the quarter to $647.3 million, compared with $509.7 million a year ago.
Total premiums for individual annuity and life rose 11.5 percent to $1.6 billion.
Mutual fund sales advanced 19 percent to $395.8 million during the opening period of 1997.

"This sharp growth in sales is indicative of the strength of The Equitable's career sales distribution system as well as the management initiatives taken last year which are now coming to fruition," McCaffrey said.
"Our move toward a financial planning orientation, redesign of our sales process and introduction of new innovative products have taken hold and are creating momentum companywide," he said.
"Additionally, sales of our Income Management family of products by our career sales force and our rapidly expanding Equitable Distributors Inc wholesaler network are exceeding our goals," he said.
Equitable chief executive Joseph Melone said the firm's overall results were boosted by the improvements in the life and annuity operations and the strength of the investment operations.

As in recent past quarters, "our continued success in the first three months of 1997 resulted from ongoing significant improvements in our annuity and insurance operations, along with outstanding performances from Equitable's investment operations, Melone said.
"Our insurance operations are now performing at a higher level of profitability and we are optimistic that this improving trend will continue," he said.
